reason: The passage contains multiple groups of regular people demonstrating clear agency through concrete actions. The Israelites take their dough (וַיִּשָּׂא הָעָם אֶת־ בְּצֵקוֹ), ask the Egyptians for items (וַֽיִּשְׁאֲלוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם), prepare and bake unleavened bread (וַיֹּאפוּ אֶת־ הַבָּצֵק), and journey out (וַיִּסְעוּ בְנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל). The Egyptians also demonstrate agency by lending items and urging the Israelites to leave. Even when following divine commands (as with 'וַיַּעֲשׂוּ כָּל־ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהוָה'), the people are clearly depicted as active agents performing these actions. Additionally, sojourners and servants are referenced with implied agency in their own observances. These are ordinary human actors, not primarily divine or mythological entities, performing deliberate actions throughout the narrative.
